question: According to the data, what is the daily free-episode limit for free users, and has it changed during 2026?

name: run_sql
purpose: Checks the observed view and catalog categories before measuring free episodes and their daily cap.
query: SELECT 'view_type' AS field, view_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS rows FROM content_views GROUP BY view_type UNION ALL SELECT 'content_tier', content_tier, COUNT(*) FROM content_catalog GROUP BY content_tier ORDER BY field, value

name: run_sql
purpose: Tests whether observed free-episode consumption has a monthly ceiling or shift during the covered 2026 period.
query: WITH daily AS (SELECT v.user_id, v.date, substr(v.date,1,7) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(v.content_id AS TEXT)||':'||CAST(v.episode_number AS TEXT)) AS free_episodes FROM content_views v WHERE v.view_type='free' GROUP BY v.user_id,v.date), months AS (SELECT month, COUNT(*) AS user_days, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users, MAX(free_episodes) AS max_free_episodes, SUM(CASE WHEN free_episodes>8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS days_over_8, SUM(CASE WHEN free_episodes=8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS days_at_8, ROUND(AVG(free_episodes),2) AS avg_free_episodes FROM daily GROUP BY month) SELECT * FROM months ORDER BY month

name: update_hypotheses

hypotheses.statement: The documented daily free-episode limit was 8 throughout 2026.
hypotheses.evidence: Business brief says 8, but observed free-viewer daily distinct-episode maxima were 5 in April–June and 8 in July–September 2026.

hypotheses.statement: The effective observed free limit increased from 5 to 8 around July 2026.
hypotheses.evidence: No free-viewer user-day exceeded 5 through June, while users reached 8 in each month from July onward; need verify exact transition and data consistency.

hypotheses.statement: The apparent change is an artifact of view categorization or episodes not matching the free catalog tier.
hypotheses.evidence: View categories found are free, sub, ppv; need cross-check free events against catalog tiers and dates.

next_step: Check the date-level transition, daily-count distributions, and whether free-tagged views consistently refer to free-tier content; the data can show effective behavior but may not document a policy setting.

name: run_sql
purpose: Identifies the precise observed transition date and verifies whether user-days ever exceed the apparent 5/8-episode ceilings.
query: WITH daily AS (SELECT v.date, v.user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(v.content_id AS TEXT)||':'||CAST(v.episode_number AS TEXT)) AS n FROM content_views v WHERE v.view_type='free' GROUP BY v.date,v.user_id), date_stats AS (SELECT date, MAX(n) AS daily_max, SUM(CASE WHEN n=5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS users_at_5, SUM(CASE WHEN n=8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS users_at_8, SUM(CASE WHEN n>8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS users_over_8 FROM daily GROUP BY date) SELECT MIN(CASE WHEN daily_max=8 THEN date END) AS first_date_max_8, MAX(CASE WHEN daily_max=5 THEN date END) AS last_date_max_5, MIN(CASE WHEN daily_max=5 THEN date END) AS first_date_max_5, MAX(CASE WHEN daily_max=8 THEN date END) AS last_date_max_8, SUM(CASE WHEN daily_max=5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dates_max_5, SUM(CASE WHEN daily_max=8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dates_max_8, SUM(CASE WHEN daily_max<5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dates_max_below_5, SUM(users_over_8) AS users_over_8 FROM date_stats

name: run_sql
purpose: Checks whether free-tagged viewing rows actually belong to free-tier content, which could otherwise distort the inferred limit.
query: SELECT v.view_type, c.content_tier, COUNT(*) AS view_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT v.user_id) AS users, MIN(v.date) AS first_date, MAX(v.date) AS last_date FROM content_views v JOIN content_catalog c ON c.content_id=v.content_id GROUP BY v.view_type,c.content_tier ORDER BY v.view_type,c.content_tier

name: update_hypotheses

hypotheses.statement: The documented daily free-episode limit was 8 throughout 2026.
hypotheses.evidence: In the observed period, the highest distinct free episodes per user-day was 5 on every date from 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30, then 8 on every date from 2026-07-01 through 2026-09-30.

hypotheses.statement: The effective observed free limit increased from 5 to 8 around July 2026.
hypotheses.evidence: The first date with a user reaching 8 was 2026-07-01; the last date with a daily maximum of 5 was 2026-06-30. No free-view user-day exceeded 8, and all daily maxima were exactly 5 or 8.

hypotheses.statement: The apparent change is an artifact of view categorization or episodes not matching the free catalog tier.
hypotheses.evidence: All 357,465 rows tagged view_type='free' matched free-tier catalog content. Subscription viewing also includes free-tier content, so view_type—not catalog tier alone—is the suitable measure of free-limit usage.

next_step: Answer with the observed 5-to-8 shift, state the database only covers April–September 2026 and has no explicit policy-change log, and distinguish observed effective limit from a documented configuration.

answer:
## Answer
In the data, the effective daily free-episode limit appears to have increased from **5 to 8 on July 1, 2026**. Free-viewing records show no user watched more than 5 distinct episodes per day through June, or more than 8 per day from July onward.

## Definition and scope
I counted distinct episodes watched per user per day where the viewing record was tagged `free`. The available viewing data covers **April 1–September 30, 2026**.

## Data quality
All free-tagged viewing records matched free-tier content. The database contains viewing activity, not an explicit history of policy settings, so the dates indicate an **observed effective limit**, not a confirmed configuration change. The data does not cover January–March or October–December 2026.
